messages:
ana: Quick note from onboarding: our Go sample that does `gen.Stream(ctx)` sometimes blocks on Close when the request has a very short deadline. Observed under token rotation and tight client deadlines.

ana: Repro: client sets ctx with 300ms deadline, we call gen.Stream(ctx) then iterate chunks. If handshake takes longer than deadline, Close blocks for >5s.

vik: Can you paste the minimal flow? suspect deadline propagation race between handshake (which does network auth refresh) and stream teardown.

ana: handler gist: func h(w,r){ ctx,_:=context.WithTimeout(r.Context(),300*time.Millisecond); s,err:=client.Generator("m").Stream(ctx,p); defer s.Close(); for c:=range s.Chunks(){ fmt.Fprint(w,c.Text) }}

sal: Two UX problems: (1) users expect Close to be bounded by the ctx deadline they provided, (2) SDK serializes token refresh under a global mutex so handshake can block many goroutines. If deadline expires, internal goroutines still wait for refresh and Close waits on them.

vik: Proposal: SDK should (A) treat handshake as separate phase using handshakeCtx that defaults to a short timeout if not provided, (B) make Close force-cancel internal goroutines immediately, and (C) document guidance: "don't use very short deadlines for stream handshake".

ana: +1. For onboarding docs let's add a short recipe and a small snippet showing explicit handshake ctx with background timeout. Also add a CI test that uses short client deadlines and rotates tokens.

ci-bot: created issue DEVEX-701: go-sdk generator handshake vs deadline parity. Added repro script and flaky test request. Assigned to @vik.

vik: I'll draft a tiny API PR: StartStream(handshakeCtx, opts...) returning Receiver with Close() that is preemptive. Will include migration note and test.
